question: In a haemodynamically stable patient with acute upper GI bleeding and no known cardiovascular disease, red cell transfusion should be initiated when haemoglobin falls below 7 g/dL.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The restrictive threshold of Hb <7 g/dL (raised to <8 g/dL in cardiovascular disease) is recommended by NICE and BSG guidelines based on high-quality RCT evidence. Liberal transfusion at higher thresholds paradoxically worsens outcomes in variceal and non-variceal bleeding.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The restrictive transfusion threshold of Hb <7 g/dL is supported by Level 1A evidence (TRIGGER and TRANSFUSE trials) and reduces re-bleeding, portal pressure elevation in varices, and overall mortality compared with liberal transfusion at <10 g/dL. In patients with ischaemic heart disease, the threshold is raised to <8 g/dL.
